data.summary: With parallel=fixed and max_parallel_tasks=20 (local layer), ddflow status prints 'parallel: 9 (fixed: ceiling 20; limited by demand (8 in flight))' next to '582 more are ready but held by the parallelism cap'. The config doc says fixed is a ceiling lowered only under load and restored; why_not_higher in core/flowcontrol.py reports demand whenever in-flight is under the limit, so the line names no reason for 9 instead of 20, and next offered only 2 items although the operator raised the limit to 20 (D-swarm-push-2026-11-05).
data.title: Fixed-mode parallel limit sits below its ceiling and blames demand while hundreds of ready items are held

chunk_findings.detail: `_slots` passes `log.read_all` (the bound method) to `FL.limit_for` instead of calling it: `FL.limit_for(repo, cfg, st, log.read_all)`. `log.read_all` is a method; `FL.limit_for` expects the event log list, so any real `next --lane` invocation will crash when `FL.limit_for` tries to iterate or use that method object, before it can return an outcome. The same file correctly calls `log.read_all()` in `_ask` when it wants the events, showing the missing parentheses here is a defect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/pull.py:63

chunk_findings.detail: A template that names a model the catalog does not know is not reported as unavailable when the template's family is known. `catalog_facts` returns the non-empty unknown model string in `LaneFacts.model`, and `gaps` only checks `if not f.model`; it never checks whether `f.family == modelreg.UNKNOWN` for a non-empty model. Given a lane whose template has `model="gpt-5-unknown"`, `family="openai"`, declared trust, and approval, `gaps` produces no model gap, so `pull_for` calls `score.pull` and can return `OFFER` for a model no catalog can vouch for, violating the stated rule that unknown lane data is unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/swarm/dispatch.py:gaps`

chunk_findings.detail: With `Bounds(note_chars=1)` and any dispatch note longer than one character, `note` returns `"..."`, whose length is 3, exceeding the `note_chars` bound. `Bounds` does not prevent values below 3, and the new `dispatch_note_chars` knob is introduced as a positive int, so a user can configure 1; the returned note then does not respect the "note's length" bound the class documents.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/swarm/dispatch.py:note`

chunk_findings.detail: The test is named `read_the_vendor_and_price_gap` but only asserts `(facts.model, facts.family, facts.vendor) == ("Qwen3-Coder", "qwen", "alibaba")` and never asserts `facts.price_gap`. A regression in `D.catalog_facts` that returns a wrong price gap would still pass the test, so the suite does not actually verify the behavior the test claims to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_dispatch.py:test_catalog_facts_read_the_vendor_and_price_gap

chunk_findings.detail: An unresolved model is still offered. `catalog_facts` sets `model` to the raw template or route string and only uses `res.family != modelreg.UNKNOWN` to pick a vendor; `gaps` treats the lane as complete whenever `f.model` is non-empty. Given a declared, digest-approved template with `model="gpt-5-ultra"` (not in the catalog) and `family="openai"` (a known vendor), `resolve` yields `UNKNOWN`, `gaps` returns `()`, and `pull_for` returns `offer` with that model. That breaks the module rule that a model nobody can vouch for is `unavailable` and is not defaulted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/dispatch.py:catalog_facts

chunk_findings.detail: The note cap is not honored below 3 characters. `text[: max(0, bounds.note_chars - 3)] + "..."` always appends three dots. Given `Bounds(note_chars=2, why_items=1)` and any decision whose note is longer than 2, `note` returns `"..."` (length 3). `claim --note` would store more than `dispatch_note_chars` allows; `note_chars=0` likewise returns `"..."` instead of `""`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/dispatch.py:note

chunk_findings.detail: The human line is a command meant to be pasted, but only the note is passed through `shlex.quote`. Given item `a b;echo pwned` and note `ok`, the text is `ddflow claim a b;echo pwned --note 'ok'`, so a shell splits the id and runs `echo`. Quote the item the same way as the note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py:_next_text

data.summary: On SW-pull, `ddflow review --gate rubber_duck,critic` ran kimi, lan-deepseek, gemini and grok. Deepseek reported 1 MEDIUM on rubber_duck and 1 HIGH, 1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW on critic, then the gates were recorded passed with gemini and grok as reviewer. `ddflow review triage SW-pull --gate critic` says there are no numbered findings on record, so a HIGH from a panel member can be neither triaged nor seen in gate status; it survives only in the job log. Here the HIGH was false, but nothing forced anyone to look.
